author: product-requirements-expert
title: Specialty directory: which veterinarians hold this specialty
summary: A read-only page lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it, shown first name then last name. All specialties render on one page with no paging. A veterinarian holding no specialty appears nowhere on it. The page is reached by its address alone; nothing links to it.
acceptance_criteria: The page is served at /specialties.html and reads only: nothing on it manages a veterinarian or a specialty.
Given the clinic's specialties, when the page is opened, then every one of them is listed by its stored name on a single page, with no paging.
Given a specialty one or more veterinarians hold, when the page is opened, then each holder appears under it as first name then last name (for example "Helen Leary").
Given a veterinarian holding no specialty, when the page is opened, then that veterinarian appears nowhere on it.
Given a specialty no veterinarian holds, when the page is opened, then the specialty is still listed, with no veterinarian under it.
Given a veterinarian holding more than one specialty, when the page is opened, then that veterinarian appears under each of them.
Given unchanged records, when the page is opened twice, then the specialties, and the veterinarians under each, appear in the same order both times.
Given no specialty stored at all, when the page is opened, then it renders as an empty list rather than failing.
Specialty names are shown as stored and are not translated.
Given every other page of the system, when each is rendered, then none of them links to the specialty directory.
The page carries the navigation every page carries, per REQ-SYS-001; any wording the page introduces is translated into every supported language, per REQ-LANG-002.
non_goals: Managing veterinarians or their specialties through the application — NG-2 is unchanged and this page is read-only
A navigation entry or a link from any other page to the specialty directory; the product owner deferred a visible entry point to a possible follow-up request
Paging, sorting controls, or filtering on the specialty page
A machine-readable representation of the specialty listing — REQ-VET-002 was withdrawn as an artifact and must not be repeated here
Searching for a specialty or a veterinarian (NG-9 unchanged)
notes: Record-ID correction: the dispatch-start at line 1 named REQ-VET-002 in error. That ID is withdrawn to the PRD's Superseded list (machine-readable vet list, withdrawn 2026-07-31) and is never reused. Line 2 is the corrected dispatch-start; line 1 has no substantive record by design, not through truncation. Boundary check: NG-2 verified unchanged in docs/prd.md — a read-only view adds no write flow. REQ-SYS-001 requires every page to carry navigation to owner search and the veterinarian directory; that is navigation ON the page and does not conflict with the owner's decision that no navigation entry points TO this page. Four questions the request left open are recorded in the PRD's Open Questions rather than escalated, each with the narrowest reading taken in the meantime: (1) visible entry point — deferred, address-only for now; (2) ordering of specialties and of veterinarians within one — only repeatability is required, not a named order; (3) a specialty nobody holds — listed with nothing under it, no explicit marker, which is the opposite tack from the veterinarian directory's 'shown as having none'; (4) heading wording — undecided, but bound by REQ-LANG-002 in all eleven bundles. Slice sizing: one deliverable surface (code plus its tests), one page, eight acceptance tests — a single inner-loop slice.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice lands entirely in the existing vet feature package and needs no new package or dependency. It is `new` rather than `covered` for one structural reason: a specialty no veterinarian holds is unreachable through today's contracts. `Vet` owns a one-way `@ManyToMany` to `Specialty`, `VetRepository` is the only reader, and no `SpecialtyRepository` exists — so the set of stored specialties cannot be obtained at all. Three new contracts close that: `SpecialtyRepository` (Spring Data read-only lookup, the `PetTypeRepository` shape), `SpecialtyDirectory` (immutable value object that groups holders under each specialty), and `SpecialtyController` (one GET surface, no request parameter). All are recorded in docs/system-design.md § Contracts, with the projection rule and the no-inbound-link fact stated in the invariants block above the table. ADR 2026-08-08-specialty-directory-projected-in-application-code records the rejected alternatives (bidirectional association; JPQL outer join). Basis for the coverage claims: direct reads of the vet package sources and the H2 schema/seed scripts — the IDE oracle is not connected in this run, so this is the weaker grep-class basis rather than a symbol resolution.
integration_points: New GET route /specialties.html served by a new `SpecialtyController` in the vet package, not a third method on `VetController`. `VetController` already serves two surfaces and the second is a Known Defect pending removal; deepening it is the wrong direction, and the naming rule prefixes a controller by the surface it serves.

`SpecialtyController` reads `SpecialtyRepository` for the full specialty set and `VetRepository.findAll()` for the veterinarians, then hands both to `SpecialtyDirectory`. Reusing the existing cached `findAll()` keeps one read path for veterinarians; do not add a second, differently-cached one.

Template `templates/vets/specialtyDirectory.html` replaces the shared layout fragment exactly as `vetList.html` does, passing a menu key that matches no `menuItem` (for example 'specialties'). This satisfies REQ-SYS-001 — the page carries navigation TO owner search and the veterinarian directory — while nothing navigates TO this page. Do not add a `menuItem` to fragments/layout.html.

Message keys: the new heading key goes into messages.properties and the nine translated bundles (de, es, fa, hi, ja, ko, pt, ru, tr). `messages_en.properties` is deliberately skipped by I18nPropertiesSyncTest's fallback rule — adding the key there is harmless but adding it to the other nine is mandatory, or checkI18nPropertyFilesAreInSync fails.

Specialty names and veterinarian names render as stored data (`th:text="${...}"`), never through `#{...}`. Only page chrome takes message keys. checkNonInternationalizedStrings scans every new HTML line for bare literal text.

`SpecialtyDirectory` is a pure type constructed from two collections, with no Spring or JPA import. It is unit-testable with real `Vet` and `Specialty` objects and no application context — that is the point of the projection, and it keeps the grouping rule out of the controller.

patterns.description: Read-only Spring Data lookup repository with an explicit ORDER BY query — the shape `SpecialtyRepository` copies. An explicit order (by name) is the cheapest way to make the repeatable-order criterion structural rather than accidental, and it matches this precedent.

Full-name rendering as `${vet.firstName + ' ' + vet.lastName}` — reuse verbatim so the two pages read the same. This is also why `SpecialtyDirectory` carries `Vet` references rather than pre-formatted name strings: name formatting stays where it already lives.

`layout (template, menu)` — the `menu` argument only selects which existing item is highlighted. An unmatched value renders the full shared nav with nothing active, which is exactly the required combination here.

Value object (In force): immutable, equality by value, defensive copies on collections. `SpecialtyDirectory` is the first non-entity domain type here, so the framework-mapped-entity exception does not cover it — it must realize the closed Domain Core properties in full.

risks.risk: The grouping and ordering logic lands in `SpecialtyController` instead of `SpecialtyDirectory`. architecture-principles.md § Pattern Catalog states the existing controller-rule deviation does not extend to new rules, so this would be a fresh violation of the Web controller row — and the Design Validation Checklist fails it.
risks.mitigation: The controller binds nothing, decides nothing, and selects a view: two repository reads in, one `SpecialtyDirectory` into the model, view name out. Every grouping, ordering, and empty-holder decision lives in the value object and is tested there without a Spring context.

risks.risk: `SpecialtyDirectory` leaks its internal collections or the mutable `Vet`/`Specialty` entities it references, breaking the immutability property that the persistence-entity exception does not extend to it.
risks.mitigation: Copy both input collections defensively at construction and expose only unmodifiable views. Referencing entities by their loaded instances is acceptable inside one read-only request; handing out a mutable list is not.

risks.risk: The repeatable-order criterion is satisfied only by accident. `VetRepository.findAll()` carries no ORDER BY, and the `@Cacheable("vets")` result makes a second render return the identical list — so a test can pass while the underlying order is database-dependent and would differ across the three supported vendors.
risks.mitigation: Make the order explicit at both levels: specialties ordered by name in the repository query, holders ordered deterministically inside `SpecialtyDirectory` (last name then first name then id). The PRD requires only repeatability, so this adds no product scope — it makes the required property structural. Test the ordering on `SpecialtyDirectory` directly, where the cache cannot mask it.

risks.risk: A reviewer or implementer 'fixes' the empty-holder case toward consistency with vetList.html, which renders `#{none}` for a veterinarian with no specialty. The PRD deliberately takes the opposite tack here: a specialty nobody holds renders with nothing under it and no marker.
risks.mitigation: No message key and no marker for the empty-holder case. The divergence is the recorded narrowest reading of an open PRD question, not an oversight — see notes.

risks.risk: REQ-VET-002 regrows: a `@ResponseBody` method, a JSON view, or a content-negotiated second route on the specialty surface.
risks.mitigation: `SpecialtyController` exposes exactly one HTML route and returns a view name. A machine-readable representation is a recorded non-goal; the existing `/vets` route is already a Known Defect pending removal and must not be used as precedent.

risks.risk: The page loads every specialty and every veterinarian on each render, with no paging by product decision. Cost grows linearly with the clinic.
risks.mitigation: Accepted for the seeded scale and recorded in the ADR's Consequences. Do not invent paging, sorting controls, or filtering — all three are explicit non-goals.

risks.risk: `SpecialtyRepository` reads are added to the `vets` cache. That cache has no eviction configured (Open Questions from the Survey, item 5), so caching a second read widens an already-open staleness question.
risks.mitigation: Leave the specialty read uncached. The page has no measured performance requirement, and the open question stays exactly as wide as it is today.

notes:
Security: this adds one unauthenticated GET, which is the application-wide baseline and not a finding under security-principles.md § Applying this section. Stating what it exposes and to whom, per the 'Widening the exposed surface' row: specialty names and veterinarian full names, to any caller — the same data /vets.html already publishes, in the inverse arrangement. No new data class is exposed. The route takes no request parameter, so it introduces no input-validation boundary; no form binding means the mass-assignment row does not apply; Thymeleaf's default escaping covers the stored names, and must not be disabled. No secret, no filesystem or resource path, no deserialization entry point.
Reliability: the only failure mode is a data-access failure on either read, which propagates to the existing error page unchanged. Empty specialty set renders an empty list, which is an acceptance criterion, not an error path.
DDD check: `SpecialtyDirectory` is a value object over `Specialty` and `Vet`, both in the same feature package and the same bounded context — no cross-context reference and no anti-corruption layer needed. Dependency direction is unchanged: vet depends on model only, no cycle introduced. No new external dependency.
Open question left standing (recorded, not escalated — the owner has stated no further product answer is coming): the heading wording for the page is undecided. The implementer picks a base wording under a new message key and translates it into the nine bundles; changing the wording later is a bundle edit, not a design change. The other three PRD open questions are absorbed by this design as written — entry point stays address-only, ordering is made deterministic without being promised as alphabetical to the reader, and the unheld specialty renders bare.
One residual design question, deliberately left to the implementer rather than fixed here: whether `noPageShouldLinkToTheSpecialtyDirectory` lives in the vet test package (the prd-entry's file_targets) or beside I18nPropertiesSyncTest in system (the precedent for whole-template-tree scans). Either placement satisfies the criterion; the test must walk all of src/main/resources/templates and assert no href or th:href resolves to the specialty route.
No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is a no-op this dispatch.

notes:
Why this record supersedes line 5. Line 5 named docs/system-design.md only under `supporting_docs`, and docs/adr/README.md nowhere. `audit-autofix`'s `_covers_path` (scripts/handoff.py:354) reads only `primary_paths` and `supporting_paths`, so both working-tree edits audited as uncovered and blocked the implementer's gate. Both paths are now in `supporting_paths`. Both edits are mine from the line-5 dispatch: the README change is the one-row index entry for the new ADR, and the system-design change is the package-structure line, two invariant paragraphs, and four Contracts rows. No code change follows from this record; the implementation is complete and build, test, checkFormat, and checkstyleMain are green. The supersession resets the review cycle by contract, which costs nothing here — no review has run for this slice.
The three implementer deviations, judged. (1) `SpecialtyRepository extends Repository`, not `JpaRepository` — CONFIRMED, and the better call. My line-5 citation of `PetTypeRepository` was for the `@Query ... ORDER BY` shape, which the implementer kept; it should not have been read as fixing the base interface. `VetRepository` in the same package extends the narrow `Repository`, and granting `save`/`delete` on a read-only page violates least privilege for no gain. The patterns array now cites `VetRepository` for the base and `PetTypeRepository` for the query shape. The full-context PetClinicIntegrationTests boots the JPQL, so the narrow base is verified working, not assumed.
(2) Holders match by specialty id, not object identity — CONFIRMED, and a defect caught. `BaseEntity` (model/BaseEntity.java:33) overrides no `equals`, so instance comparison is reference comparison, and `VetRepository.findAll()` is `@Cacheable("vets")`: a cache hit returns `Vet` graphs holding `Specialty` instances from a closed persistence context, while `SpecialtyRepository` returns fresh ones. Reference matching would have rendered every specialty unheld on the second and every later render — a bug the acceptance tests would likely have missed, since a `@WebMvcTest` never populates the cache. Rejecting a listed specialty that carries no id is the right fail-closed reading: the directory lists stored specialties, and one without an id is a programming error, not data. This constraint is durable and non-obvious, so this dispatch crystallized it: one state sentence in docs/system-design.md § Contracts invariants and one Consequences bullet in the ADR.
(3) The directory preserves the specialty order it is given and sorts holders by last name, first name, id — CONFIRMED. The holder comparator is exactly the line-5 mitigation. Preserving rather than re-sorting the specialties is a refinement, not a departure: the repository query is then the single place fixing that order, and the constructor's javadoc states the contract to the caller. The risks entry above is updated to record the coupling.
Accepted without correction, noted for the reviewer: `SpecialtyDirectory.Entry` as a nested type name. The naming table's "never `Entry` or `Record`" binds a concept the vocabulary names; docs/ubiquitous-language.md defines "Specialty directory" but no term for one specialty plus its holders, and "directory entry" reads as the domain noun. Revisit only if the vocabulary later names that pairing.
Security, reliability, and DDD findings from line 5 stand unchanged: one unauthenticated GET at the application-wide baseline, exposing specialty names and veterinarian full names — the same data /vets.html already publishes, inverted; no request parameter and no form binding, so no new input-validation boundary and no mass-assignment surface; Thymeleaf default escaping covers the stored names; the only failure mode is a data-access failure on either read, propagating to the existing error page; `SpecialtyDirectory` is a value object over two types in the same bounded context, so no anti-corruption layer applies and the dependency direction is unchanged.
The PRD open question on heading wording stands: the implementer picked a base wording under a new message key, and changing it later is a bundle edit, not a design change.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: Nested type `SpecialtyDirectory.Entry` violates the explicit naming rule in docs/architecture-principles.md § Naming: 'the code says FeedItem, never Entry or Record.' The implementer's argument (no ubiquitous-language term exists for 'one specialty plus its holders', so inventing one oversteps implementer scope) is procedurally sound, but the conclusion does not follow: the rule is unconditional on the word `Entry`, and the system-design-expert flagged rather than resolved it at design-block line 9. This is a naming/vocabulary decision for the domain owner, not a judgment call for the reviewer or a mechanical rename for the implementer.

approved_aspects: SpecialtyDirectory correctly treated as the first non-entity domain value object: both constructor inputs are defensively copied (List.copyOf) and both getEntries()/getHolders() hand out only the copied unmodifiable views; entities themselves (Specialty, Vet) are referenced not copied, matching the design rationale in the class Javadoc
No grouping/aggregation logic leaked into SpecialtyController; it delegates entirely to SpecialtyDirectory's constructor and stays a thin GET handler

SpecialtyRepository extends the narrow Repository (not JpaRepository) with an explicit `ORDER BY specialty.name` in the @Query, matching the confirmed design and the PetTypeRepository-style read-only shape
HOLDER_ORDER comparator and the fixed repository ORDER BY give deterministic rendering, documented with the reasoning in Javadoc rather than left implicit
./gradlew checkFormat and compileJava both pass clean on the change set

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Output escaping: specialtyDirectory.html renders every database-sourced value through th:text (entry.specialty.name, holder.firstName/lastName) with Thymeleaf's default HTML escaping on. Swept the whole template for th:utext, inlined expressions ([[${...}]] / [(${...})]), javascript: URLs, event-handler attributes, and DOM injection - none present. Page chrome uses #{} message keys only; the ten added bundle values are literal headings with no expression or format-specifier content.

No injection surface: the single JPQL string in SpecialtyRepository.findSpecialties is a compile-time constant with no parameters and no concatenation; ORDER BY specialty.name is a fixed literal, not a caller-supplied sort key. The route takes no path variable, no request parameter, and no request body, so no request-derived value reaches the query - confirmed against SpecialtyController.showSpecialtyDirectory(Model), whose only argument is the model.

Mass assignment / binding: no @ModelAttribute, no form-backed type, no WebDataBinder on the new controller. The GET is read-only and the repository extends the narrow Repository rather than JpaRepository, so no save or delete capability is exposed on Specialty - least privilege honoured rather than merely unused.

Exposed surface: one new unauthenticated GET (/specialties.html) rendering specialty names and veterinarian full names. Both classes of data are already published by the existing /vets.html surface, so the change does not widen the baseline in docs/system-design.md Security Context. Per docs/security-principles.md the absence of authentication and CSRF is the demonstration's recorded shape, and URL-only reachability is correctly treated as a product decision, not a control.

Error paths: the only new exception is IllegalArgumentException in SpecialtyDirectory.identityOf, whose message carries a specialty name - stored, non-sensitive data the page itself renders. No credential, connection string, session identifier, or internal path reaches the error page. Secret sweep over the new Java, template, and bundle files for password/secret/token/key/credential returned nothing.

Supply chain: git diff over build.gradle, settings.gradle, gradle.properties, and gradle/ is empty - no dependency added, no version moved, no repository or plain-HTTP check altered. The four dependency checks in system-design.md are not engaged by this change.

Unbounded result set assessed and not recorded as a finding: two full-table reads (specialties, plus the already-cached VetRepository.findAll) render on one page. At the clinic-scale data volume this feature targets, an anonymous request costs no more than the existing /vets.html read path, so no-pagination is a product decision with no denial-of-service consequence at this scale. Worth revisiting only if specialty or veterinarian counts leave clinic scale.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: Every test in both files constructs one Specialty instance and passes that same object reference into both the specialties collection and vet.addSpecialty(...) (via createASpecialty/createAVetHolding + Vet::addSpecialty). SpecialtyDirectory.identityOf/holdersBySpecialtyId match holders by Specialty.getId(), precisely because the ADR (docs/adr/2026-08-08-specialty-directory-projected-in-application-code.md) states the two reads return separate Specialty instances under the real cached VetRepository, and Specialty inherits no equals(). None of the 11 tests exercise that scenario: because the same instance is shared, a regression from id-based matching to reference matching (held == specialty) would still pass every test in the suite. This is the exact bug the design re-triage flagged as a risk, and the suite as written would not catch it. No test in SpecialtyDirectoryTests constructs two directories/entries to compare for equality; the one equals-based assertion in SpecialtyControllerTests (model().attribute with an empty SpecialtyDirectory) only exercises the trivial empty-list case. The two-distinct-Specialty-instances-same-id test requested above would also close most of this gap (its assertion path runs through Entry.equals for holder membership); add a small direct SpecialtyDirectoryTests case for the equals/hashCode contract itself (equal-by-content but different instance, unequal entries, wrong type) so the value object's identity contract is verified, not just incidentally exercised.
findings.fix: Add unit tests in SpecialtyDirectoryTests for SpecialtyDirectory/Entry equals() and hashCode(): reflexivity (self-equals), two directories built from equal-content-but-distinct entries are equal, a directory with a different entry is not, and equals(nonSpecialtyDirectoryObject) is false.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Specialty directory: which veterinarians hold this specialty
summary: A read-only page lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it, shown first name then last name. All specialties render on one page with no paging. A veterinarian holding no specialty appears nowhere on it. The page is reached by its address alone; nothing links to it.
acceptance_criteria: The page is served at /specialties.html and reads only: nothing on it manages a veterinarian or a specialty.
Given the clinic's specialties, when the page is opened, then every one of them is listed by its stored name on a single page, with no paging.
Given a specialty one or more veterinarians hold, when the page is opened, then each holder appears under it as first name then last name (for example "Helen Leary").
Given a veterinarian holding no specialty, when the page is opened, then that veterinarian appears nowhere on it.
Given a specialty no veterinarian holds, when the page is opened, then the specialty is still listed, with no veterinarian under it.
Given a veterinarian holding more than one specialty, when the page is opened, then that veterinarian appears under each of them.
Given unchanged records, when the page is opened twice, then the specialties, and the veterinarians under each, appear in the same order both times.
Given no specialty stored at all, when the page is opened, then it renders as an empty list rather than failing.
Specialty names are shown as stored and are not translated.
Given every other page of the system, when each is rendered, then none of them links to the specialty directory.
The page carries the navigation every page carries, per REQ-SYS-001; any wording the page introduces is translated into every supported language, per REQ-LANG-002.
non_goals: Publishing the specialty listing in a machine-readable form alongside the page — now recorded in docs/prd.md as NG-10
Managing veterinarians or their specialties through the application — NG-2 is unchanged and this page is read-only
A navigation entry or a link from any other page to the specialty directory; the product owner deferred a visible entry point to a possible follow-up request
Paging, sorting controls, or filtering on the specialty page
Searching for a specialty or a veterinarian (NG-9 unchanged)

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Resolves the code-quality-reviewer's clarify finding at SpecialtyDirectory.java:130. The design of the slice is unchanged from the record at line 9 — same three contracts, same projection rule, same identity-matching invariant, same routes. The only change is a name. integration_points: No contract in docs/system-design.md names the nested type. The Contracts row for `SpecialtyDirectory` (system-design.md:109) and the invariant paragraph (system-design.md:82) describe the projection without naming its element type, and the ADR names only `SpecialtyDirectory`. The rename therefore needs no edit to docs/system-design.md or the ADR — confirmed by grep over both files for `SpecialtyDirectory`.

patterns.description: **Listed specialty** and **Holder**, added this dispatch. `ListedSpecialty` is the code name for the first; `getHolders()` and the `holders` locals already realize the second, which is why the term is added alongside — the same naming rule binds that word and it was equally unnamed.

Naming table, row 'Value objects, aggregates: Domain noun, no suffix'. `ListedSpecialty` is a domain noun with a qualifying adjective and no suffix. `Entry` is not a domain noun; `SpecialtyListing` or `SpecialtyRecord` would carry a container suffix and fail the same row.

risks.risk: The rename is applied by search-and-replace and catches `java.util.Map.Entry`, which is unrelated. It appears at src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/system/I18nPropertiesSyncTest.java:115, and `containsEntry` appears twice in CrashControllerIntegrationTests.
risks.mitigation: Rename by symbol, not by text. The only symbols in scope are the nested type `SpecialtyDirectory.Entry`, the field `entries`, the accessor `getEntries()`, and their local and template bindings. Every JDK `Map.Entry` and every AssertJ `containsEntry` stays as it is.

risks.risk: `ListedSpecialty` is read as naming a Specialty that someone holds, making the zero-holder case sound contradictory — the same trap that ruled out `HeldSpecialty`.
risks.mitigation: The adjective is 'listed', not 'held': the directory lists a specialty whether or not anyone holds it. The vocabulary entry states the may-be-none case in its definition, and the type's existing javadoc already says the same. Keep that javadoc sentence.

notes:
The literal instruction. In src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/vet/SpecialtyDirectory.java: nested type `Entry` -> `ListedSpecialty` (declaration at :130, private constructor at :136, the `instanceof Entry entry` pattern at :155 -> `instanceof ListedSpecialty listed`); field `entries` -> `listedSpecialties` (:53, :70, :113, :118, :123); accessor `getEntries()` -> `getListedSpecialties()` (:76); the `List<Entry>` types at :53, :66, :76 and the `new Entry(...)` at :68 follow. The local named `listed` at :66 becomes `paired` or similar to avoid colliding with the new pattern variable — implementer's choice, it is a local. In src/main/resources/templates/vets/specialtyDirectory.html:18: `th:each="entry : ${specialtyDirectory.entries}"` -> `th:each="listed : ${specialtyDirectory.listedSpecialties}"`, then `entry.specialty.name` -> `listed.specialty.name` and `entry.holders` -> `listed.holders`. In src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/vet/SpecialtyDirectoryTests.java: `getEntries()` -> `getListedSpecialties()` at :59, :87, :100, :116, :137; `SpecialtyDirectory.Entry::getHolders` -> `SpecialtyDirectory.ListedSpecialty::getHolders` at :87; the lambda parameter `entry` at :100 and :116 -> `listed`. Test names and assertions keep their current intent; a test name reading 'entry' in the BDD sense of a directory row may be reworded to 'listed specialty' but no assertion changes.
Why rename rather than defend `Entry`. The reviewer and the implementer are each half right, and the finding is correctly routed here. The implementer is right that the vocabulary named no concept, and that inventing one oversteps implementer scope. The reviewer is right that the conclusion does not follow, because the rule's remedy for a missing term is to name it, not to fall back on a container word. Naming it is my call to make, so I make it. Note also that the concept was never truly nameless: docs/prd.md already says 'each with the veterinarians holding it' and 'every one of them is listed', and the ADR says 'pairing every specialty with its holders'. `ListedSpecialty` is assembled from words the requirement already uses, which is what the naming rule asks for.
Brief defect, surfaced not overridden. docs/architecture-principles.md:115 reads 'Names come from the project's canonical vocabulary: if the PRD calls it a "feed item", the code says `FeedItem`, never `Entry` or `Record`.' Two readings are available. Read as a provenance rule, the trailing clause illustrates the failure mode and binds only when the vocabulary has a term. Read as the reviewer read it, the clause bans two words outright. The brief has a dedicated mechanism for outright word bans — the Prohibited suffixes list at :134 — and `Entry` is absent from it, which is evidence for the first reading. The sentence should say which it means. I cannot fix it: docs/architecture-principles.md is outside my write scope. Recorded here for its owner. The resolution above needs no ruling, because renaming satisfies both readings; the ruling would only have mattered had I kept `Entry`.
Names considered and rejected. `HeldSpecialty` — false for the zero-holder case the requirement explicitly protects. `SpecialtyListing`, `SpecialtyRecord`, `Row` — container suffixes, the same class of word as `Entry`. `SpecialtyRoster` — docs/prd.md already uses 'roster' for the full veterinarian list ('lists specialties, not the full roster'), so it would collide. `SpecialtyTeam`, `Panel` — assert an organizational structure the clinic does not have. `SpecialtyHolders` — stutters as `SpecialtyDirectory.SpecialtyHolders`, and plural type names read badly in `List<...>`. All are listed on the vocabulary entry's Avoid line where they are drift risks.
No `supersedes_record_at`, deliberately. The schema (design-block.schema.json:126) and route-spec.md:157 both scope supersession to a true re-triage, and setting it voids the round's approvals — including security-reviewer's clean pass at line 18, whose subject is unaffected by a rename. The design at line 9 stands; this record revises one naming judgment inside it and the fix loop re-reviews the changed files through the normal changes_requested path. Line 9's closing note, which accepted `Entry` without correction, is superseded in substance by this record as the latest design-block for the slice.
Path coverage. `_covers_path` (scripts/handoff.py:354) reads `primary_paths` and `supporting_paths` only, and its dirty scan covers docs/system-design.md and docs/adr/ — docs/ubiquitous-language.md falls outside that scan but is listed in `supporting_paths` anyway, since it is the one doc this dispatch edited. The three docs edited under line 9 and still uncommitted are carried forward in `supporting_paths` so coverage does not depend on which design-block the audit reaches first.
Autofix audit: the log holds no `design-doc-autofix` records, so the audit is a no-op this dispatch, as it was at line 9.
Process slip, recorded for the audit trail: I read the handoff log and the review-feedback in three tool calls before appending `dispatch-start`, which belongs first. No record was written before it and nothing downstream is affected, but the dispatch-event contract was momentarily broken.
